subject: Archaeology
subcategory: Lost Cities of the Ancient World
title: Heracleion: Egypt's Sunken Port
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Heracleion: Egypt's Sunken Port.

hook.text: An entire Egyptian port city lay hidden under the Mediterranean Sea for 1,200 years before divers found it.

buildup.text: Heracleion was Egypt's main trading port before Alexandria was built. Greek historians described it as magnificent.

discovery.text: In 2000, Franck Goddio found temples, giant statues, and 64 ships lying on the seabed in Abu Qir Bay.

twist.text: The city sank because it was built on unstable clay. Earthquakes and rising seas did the rest over centuries.

climax.text: Divers pulled up a five-meter granite statue of a pharaoh from the mud — perfectly preserved by the cold dark water.

punchline.text: The sea swallowed a city whole and kept it in near-perfect condition.

quiz.question: Why did the ancient city of Heracleion sink?
options: A massive tsunami overwhelmed the city in a single event
It was built on unstable clay that gave way during earthquakes
Rising sea levels from melting glaciers flooded the coastline

details.summary: Heracleion, ancient Egypt's greatest port city, sank beneath Abu Qir Bay near Alexandria after earthquakes and liquefaction around the 8th century CE. Rediscovered underwater in 2000 by Franck Goddio, its submerged temples, colossal statues, and hundreds of ships reveal a major trade center.
details.whyItMatters: Heracleion was one of antiquity's most important ports, yet it was lost for over a thousand years. Its underwater discovery proved that entire ancient cities lie beneath the sea, waiting for technology to find them.
takeaways: Ancient Egypt's major port city, sunk by earthquakes and liquefaction
Submerged temples, colossal statues, and hundreds of ships found

faq.question: How did an entire city sink beneath the sea?
faq.answer: Heracleion was built on unstable clay and sand sediments in the Nile Delta. Earthquakes caused liquefaction — solid ground turning to fluid — which catastrophically lowered the land surface. Tidal wave flooding completed the submersion.

faq.question: What has been found at Heracleion's underwater site?
faq.answer: Over 64 ancient ships, a temple to Amun-Gereb, colossal granite statues of pharaohs and gods, gold coins, bronze ritual objects, and hundreds of inscriptions. The finds confirm Heracleion's role as Egypt's primary international trading port before Alexandria was founded.
